text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein stresses need to complete building peace. Prime Minister Kabariti says Israel's building of settlements "threatens directly the security of Jordan."
- Crown Prince Hassan says "peace and security go hand in hand and do not thrive in the shadow of oppression."
- Finance committee studies a proposal to raise salaries of public sector employees.
- Stocks in downward trend, a large bloc sale pushes turnover to a 3.3 million dinar ($4.6 million) high.

- King Hussein, in an interview with Israel's Channel Two television, says he "hopes that a new war in the region will not flare," emphasises that accords are "sacrosanct and extremists are dictating the agenda."
- King and Kabariti meet the EU's new Middle East envoy.
- Kabariti says unique achievements made in Jordan and the opposition are a major party in the democratic scene.
- Information Minister Muasher visits Israel to discuss the peace process.
- King Hussein says he "blesses a Palestinian state and supports its creation and I will help it if this is the Palestinians' desire."
- Jordan's share of the Iraqi market in oil-for-food-deal is dependant on quality and prices not politics. The stock market takes a pause after exhaustion with year-end selling.
- Anti-corruption drive knows no distinction -- General Intelligence Director officer.
- Kabariti, in a seminar marking International Human Rights day, urges objectivity and studies before levelling human rights charges.
- Kabariti, Iraqi trade minister discuss relations, trade.
